Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:10:1.hebrew: הראני פרסיים - בעל משלות ודומיות היה לוי, וקאמר לו רבי: משול לי פרסיים, למה הם דומים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:10:1.english: Show me Persians - Levi was skilled in analogies and comparisons, and Rabbi said to him: Draw an analogy for me [regarding] Persians — to what are they similar?

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:10:2.english: Like the legions of the house of David - [They are] mighty.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:10:3.hebrew: חברין - אומה הסמוכה לפרסיים, ומשחיתים הם וטרפנים הם יותר מפרסיים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:10:3.english: Ḥabbarin - A nation adjacent to the Persians; and they are destructive and predatory, more so than the Persians.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:10:4.english: To demons - [They are] dressed in black and resemble demons.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:10:5.hebrew: דומים למלאכי השרת - לבושים לבנים ועטופים כמלאכי השרת, וכתיב (יחזקאל ט) והאיש לבוש הבדים. והכי נמי אמרינן בבמה מדליקין (שבת דף כה:) על רבי יהודה שהיה מתעטף ויושב בסדינים המצוייצין ודומה למלאך כו'. ובנדרים (דף כ:) נמי אמרינן: מאן מלאכי השרת? רבנן. ואמאי קרי להו מלאכי השרת? משום דמצויינין כמלאכי השרת במלבושים נאים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:10:5.english: They are similar to ministering angels - [They are] dressed in white and cloaked like ministering angels. And it is written (Ezekiel 9): "And the man clothed in linen." And so too we say in [the chapter entitled] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 25b) regarding Rabbi Yehuda, who would cloak himself and sit in fringed sheets, and was similar to an angel, etc. And in Nedarim (20b) we also say: Who are the ministering angels? The Rabbis. And why are they called ministering angels? Because they are distinguished like ministering angels with handsome garments.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:11:1.english: When he was dying - Prophecy was cast into his mouth.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:11:2.english: Homanya - A city whose name is such.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:11:3.hebrew: מסגריא - עיר היא, וכל הנך כולהו מקומות נינהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:11:3.english: Masgariya - It is a city, and all of these are places.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:11:4.hebrew: בירתא דסטיא - על שם שסרו מאחרי המקום, ופירש רבי היאך סרו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:11:4.english: Bireta DeSatya - [It is so called] on account of [the fact] that they turned away from the Omnipresent; and Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] explained how they turned away:

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:11:5.hebrew: דאקפי פירא דכוורי ואזיל וציידי בשבתא ושמתינהו וכו' - הציף הביבר (ויביי"ר: ברכת דגים) דגים הרבה, והלכו וצדו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:11:5.english: That a fish pond overflowed with fish, and they went and caught [them] on Shabbat, and he excommunicated them, etc. - The fish preserve (*vivier*: a fish pond) cast up many fish, and they went and caught [them].

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:11:6.hebrew: דאקפי - הציף, כדמתרגמינן "ויצף הברזל" (מלכים ב ו׳:ו׳) — "וקפא פרזלא":
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:11:6.english: That overflowed - Overflowed, as we translate: “And the iron floated” (II Kings 6:6) — “u-khefa parzela.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:11:7.hebrew: פירא - בריכה עשויה לגדל דגים, ובלע"ז ביבר (ויביי"ר: ברכת דגים):
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:11:7.english: A ditch - A pond made to raise fish, and in Old French: bivar (vivier: a fishpond).

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:11:8.english: And they became apostates - They apostatized.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:1:1.hebrew: והאידנא הוא דליוה פרסאי - שלקחוהו ממקומו ובנאוהו למעלה מאקרא. ולהכי לא בעי "לתחת פרת עד היכן?", לפי שפרת נופל בחדקל, ועוד: בבל מושכת למטה ממנו עד אפמיא תתאה, כדאמר לעיל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:1:1.english: And it is now that the Persians moved it up - That they took it from its place and built it higher up than the fortress. And for this reason [the Gemara] did not ask, "Until where downward on the Euphrates?", because the Euphrates flows into the Tigris, and furthermore, Babylonia extends below it until Lower Appamya, as [the Gemara] said above.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:1:2.hebrew: להך גיסא דפרת עד היכא - בשפתה כלפי מערב, עד היכן מתפשט רחבה של בבל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:1:2.english: On that side of the Euphrates, until where? - On its bank toward the west, how far does the width of Babylonia extend?

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:1:3.english: What is your thinking - That you have come to ask?

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:1:4.english: Due to Biram - Perhaps Biram, which is situated on that side, is what you are asking about.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:1:5.hebrew: מייחסי דפומבדיתא - שהיא בין שתי הנהרות — מבירם נסבי. ש"מ: מוחזקים הם בה בחזקת יחוס:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:1:5.english: Those of pure lineage of Pumbedita - which is between the two rivers — marry [women] from Biram. Conclude from this: they are held in it to have the presumption of [pure] lineage.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:2:1.english: Just as [there is] a dispute with regard to lineage - Regarding the length and breadth of Babylonia.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:2:2.hebrew: כך מחלוקת לגיטין - דקיימא לן (גיטין דף ב.): המביא גט משאר ארצות צריך שיאמר "בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם", לפי שאין בקיאין לשמה. והמביא גט מארץ ישראל לבבל אינו צריך לומר, ובבל הרי היא כארץ ישראל לגיטין — שאף הם היו חכמים ובקיאין לשמה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:2:2.english: So is there a dispute with regard to bills of divorce - For it is established for us (Gittin 2a): One who brings a bill of divorce from other lands must say, "In my presence it was written and in my presence it was signed," because they are not expert [in writing it] for her sake. And one who brings a bill of divorce from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia does not need to say [this], and Babylonia is like Eretz Yisrael with regard to bills of divorce — since they, too, were scholars and expert [in writing it] for her sake.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:2:3.hebrew: עד ארבא תניינא - אגם של קנים וערבה, שקורין אושר"א:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:2:3.english: Up to the second arba - A marsh of reeds and willows, which they call osieraie [an osier bed].

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:2:4.hebrew: תניינא דגישרא - שני אגמים היו למטה מהגשר, זה למטה מזה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:2:4.english: The second [lake] of the bridge - There were two lakes below the bridge, one below the other:

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:3:1.english: Ḥaveil Yamma - The name of a place.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:3:2.english: The glory of Babylonia - The crown and splendor of Babylonia with regard to lineage.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:3:3.english: Shunya and Guvya and Tzitzora - They are places.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:3:4.english: The glory of Ḥaveil Yamma - The splendor of Ḥaveil Yamma.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:3:5.hebrew: איתתא בעא מינייהו - כותיים לא נתערבו בהם, אבל הקול יצא על ידי ששאל כותי אחד אשה מהם, אבל הם לא נתנו לו. ויש אומרים: רב פפא בעא מנייהו איתתא ולא יהבי ליה, לכך היה מוציא עליהם שמץ פסול; וקשה בעיני לומר כן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:3:5.english: A woman he requested from them - Samaritans did not assimilate with them, but the rumor went out because one Samaritan requested a woman from them, but they did not give [her] to him. And some say: Rav Pappa requested a woman from them and they did not give [her] to him, [and] therefore he cast a taint of disqualification upon them; but it is difficult in my view to say so.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:4:1.english: Like the exile - [The Gemara] calls Pumbedita "the exile" in Rosh Hashanah (23b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:4:2.hebrew: והאמר ר' יוחנן - לעיל, מיחסותא דבבל בפרת: עד מעברתא דגדמא, ותו לא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:4:2.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say - Earlier, regarding the lineage of Babylonia along the Euphrates: Until the ferry crossing of Gadma, and no further.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:4:3.hebrew: מאיהי דקירא - מקום על נהר פרת, למעלה מכל המקומות הנזכרים למעלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:4:3.english: From Ihi Dekira - A place on the Euphrates River, upstream from all the places mentioned above.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:4:4.hebrew: והאמר ר' יוחנן - לעיל, מיחסותא דבבל בפרת, עד מעברתא דגדמא, ותו לא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:4:4.english: But doesn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan say - Earlier, regarding the lineage of Babylonia along the Euphrates: Until the crossing of Gidma, and no further.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:4:5.hebrew: אמר אביי רצועה נפקא - באלכסון ממעברתא דגדמא, ומקפת את הפסולין עד מעלה מאיהי דקירא — שהי' מן הפסולין — ושוט משוט בפי הרצועה על פרת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:4:5.english: Abaye said: A strip extends - Diagonally from the crossing of Gizma, and it goes around the disqualified [areas] up to above Ihi Dekira — which was among the disqualified [places] — and Shot Mishot is at the tip of the strip, on the Euphrates.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:4:6.hebrew: אמר אביי רצועה נפקא - באלכסון ממעברתא דגדמא, ומקפת את הפסולין עד מעלה מאיהי דקירא — שהי' מן הפסולין — ושוט משוט בפי הרצועה על פרת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:4:6.english: Abaye said: A strip extends - Diagonally from the crossing at Gizma, and it skirts the disqualified [areas] until above Ihi Dekira — which is [itself] among the disqualified [places] — and Shot Mishot is at the tip of the strip, on the Euphrates.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:6:1.english: And he put them in Halah and in Habor - [The verse] is speaking of the ten tribes whom Sennacherib exiled.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:7:1.hebrew: וכולן לפסול - כל מקום שגלו השבטים, נטמעו עובדי כוכבים בבנותיהם. ועובד כוכבים ועבד הבא על בת ישראל — אפילו למ"ד (יבמות דף מה.) הולד ממזר לא הוי — פגום מיהא הוי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:7:1.english: And all of them are with regard to flawed lineage - In every place to which the [Ten] Tribes were exiled, idolaters intermingled with their daughters. And [regarding] an idolater or a slave who has relations with a Jewish woman — even according to the one who says (Yevamot 45a) that the offspring is not a mamzer — [the offspring] is at any rate disqualified [from the priesthood].

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:8:1.hebrew: ותלת עלעין בפומה - בחיה השניה שבמראה דניאל כתיב, והיא בבל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:8:1.english: “And it had three ribs in its mouth” - [This] is written concerning the second beast in Daniel’s vision, and it is Babylonia:

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:8:2.hebrew: בפומה בין שיניה - בפומה משמע מבפנים, בין שיניה משמע שבולטות מבחוץ:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:8:2.english: In its mouth between its teeth - “In its mouth” implies [that they are] inside; “between its teeth” implies that they protrude on the outside.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:9:1.hebrew: ומסורבלים כדוב - בעלי בשר. לשון עובי ושומן הוא. ובעלמא (שבת דף קלז:) נמי אמרי': "קטן מסורבל בבשר" — המלובש בבשר כסרבל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:9:1.english: And corpulent like a bear - Fleshy [people]. It is an expression of thickness and fatness. And elsewhere (Shabbat 137b), we also say: "An infant enveloped in flesh" — who is clothed in flesh like a cloak.

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:9:2.hebrew: דוב אין לו מנוחה - כשהוא קשור, הולך ובא תמיד סביבותיו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:9:2.english: A bear has no rest - When it is tied up, it constantly paces back and forth around itself:

Rashi on Kiddushin 72a:9:3.english: A bear on the move - A wandering bear.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 72a:1:1.hebrew: להך גיסא דפרת עד היכן - פי' בקונטרס: להכי לא בעי לתחת פרת עד היכא — לפי שפרת נופל בחדקל; ועוד, בבל מושכת למטה ממנו עד אפמיא תתאה, כדאמר לעיל:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 72a:1:1.english: "To that side of the Euphrates, until where" - [Rashi] explained in the commentary: For this reason [the Gemara] did not ask, "Downward on the Euphrates, until where?" — because the Euphrates flows into the Tigris; and furthermore, Babylonia extends downward below it until Lower Apamea, as [the Gemara] said earlier.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 72a:3:1.hebrew: איתתא בעא מינייהו ולא יהבו ליה - ולכך הוציא עליהם לעז. וי"מ דקאי אדרב פפא, ולא נהירא — דח"ו שיעלה בדעתו של אותו צדיק להוציא לעז עליהם שלא כדין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 72a:3:1.english: "He sought a woman from them and they did not give [her] to him" - And therefore he spread slander against them. And some explain that [this] refers to Rav Pappa; but this is not plausible, for heaven forbid that it would enter the mind of that righteous man to spread slander against them unjustly.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 72a:4:1.hebrew: בין הנהרות הרי היא כגולה ליוחסין - וצריך לומר דשני מקומות הן, דאי משום חדקל ופרת — לא הוה בעי גמרא: "וכי בין הנהרות מאי הוי?", דפשיטא לכולי עלמא דמייחסי; דלעיל נמי לא בעי אלא מן הצדדין, אבל בין הנהרות — פשיטא ליה דמיוחסין הן:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 72a:4:1.english: "Between the rivers is like the exile with regard to lineage" - And one must say that these are two [different] places, for if [it were] on account of the Tigris and the Euphrates, the Gemara would not have asked: "And if it is located between the rivers, what of it?", as it is obvious to everyone that they are of unflawed lineage; for above as well, [the Gemara] only inquired regarding the [outer] sides, but [as for the area] between the rivers, it was obvious to it that they are of unflawed lineage.
